items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Jack Crystal who worked in Milt's record shop was in charge of the session which featured many well known black and white musicians: ... Bobby Hackett ... to name a few that participated in these sessions

ctx.x: I gigged and did many Sunday afternoon jam sessions at Jimmy Ryan's and few in Boston at the Ken Club. Once in Boston I jammed with Pete Brown and another time with Coleman Hawkins. The sessions at Jimmy Ryan's which was across the street from the Famous Door and the three Dances on 52nd Street, were presented by Milt Gabler who owned the Commodore Record Shop near the Grand Central station on East 42nd Street.

Jack Crystal who worked in Milt's record shop was in charge of the session which featured many well known black and white musicians: Art Hodes, Pee Wee Russell, Bobby Hackett, George Wettling, Rod Cless, Sid Catlett, Hank Duncan, Sandy Williams, Wild Bill Davison and Oran "Hot Lips" Page to name a few that participated in these sessions which really jumped. There were always two bottles of whisky furnished by Milt to get the sessions in a swinging mood. The closing number was always 'Bugle Call Rag' and I'm…

One day, Al Hall came to my house and asked me if I would like to replace a guitarist named Billy Moore who was sick in a hospital. My brother(who was a tailor) and I were sharing a three-roomed furnished apartment on 161st Street and I had not seen Al for quite some time. He told me that he was working at the Cafe Society Uptown with Billy Moore and a pianist.
